findings.summary: When options.encoding is set, the Accept-Encoding check is skipped, so responses get compressed with an encoding the client may not accept (or sent no header for), producing unreadable responses.
Same change in the Deno dist copy: options.encoding bypasses the Accept-Encoding check, so responses may be compressed with an encoding the client doesn't accept.
Substring matching on Accept-Encoding with includes() ignores q=0, so 'gzip;q=0' (not acceptable) still matches; this flaw pre-existed.
Same substring matching issue in the Deno dist copy: q=0 in Accept-Encoding is ignored.
